Voat, what genre of music would you like to get into, but you don't know where to start? Voaters who listen to those kinds of music, what would you recommend?

I always kind of wanted to get into country music, but there's an awful lot of it and supposedly there's a lot of BAD country music mixed in. I liked the stuff that was in GTA San Andreas a lot, if that helps.

Well, the best place to start is where you're currently at. Look at the music you like currently, and then look for strains of it in other genres.

For me, I grew up listening to blues records when I was kid. (I'm old. Leave me alone.) Most of my tastes derived from that. The blues roots of rock were what made me love the Stones, but not give a damn about the Beatles. Those blues roots fed into my love of motown and soul, then punk. At the time I grew up, country acts were on Hee Haw, a bad show on television with polyester clad idiots singing over produced country. I hated it. It would be later in life that I would love country.

Keep in mind that rock, hip hop, soul and country all come from the same roots, the mixture of Scotch Irish Americana and rhythms from black American culture. This synthesis met head on in the mid 19th century, creating the roots of almost every popular form of music today.

Anyways, country primer 101.

One of the greats to start with is Johnny Cash. He best exemplifies country's unique dichotomy between the sinner and the saint. Listen to him covering a Nine Inch Nails song, Hurt. If it doesn't punch you in the gut, you have no soul. Move on to his best album, Live At Folsom Prison. Cocaine Blues is a great track.

From there move on to George Jones, Hank Williams sr., and Patsy Cline.

These acts represent the stock on which to build your musical stew. Classic standards from when country was coming into it's own.

The next step might be to look back a little bit. Understand the bluegrass roots of country. I'm listening to Sierra Hull right now. There's so much great stuff out there. It's a little bit of spice and sugar to your stew.

Now to add your own ingredients. There's a bunch of great stuf when you get out of country pop. You have bands like the Turnpike Troubadours (I love the song every girl. Really beautiful song.) There's, of course, Hank Williams III. Long tradition, but he's going back to the rebel roots of country. Listen to Moonshiner's Life. There's bands like Hellbound Glory. I dig the song Either way we're fucked. Birdcloud, with Fuck you cop is just dumb redneck rampage stuff.

Then there's stuff that's out there. I love Gangstagrass They combine country, bluegrass and hip hop. Great in concert.
Honestly, just making music in general. I really have no idea where to start. I'm interested in playing the harmonica (played around for about a year) and musical saw
Blues Traveler has a great harmonica-ist (?) and actually blues in general is where you should start
